questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The word systematics is derived from the Latin word 'systema' which means?
questions.solution: tic arrangement of organisms. Linnaeus used Systema Naturae as the title of his publication.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: _________ are useful in providing information for identification of varieties of species found in an area.
questions.solution: Flora contains the actual account of the habitat and distribution of plants in a given area. These provide the index to the plant species found in a particular area. Manuals are useful in providing information for the identification of names of species found in an area. Monographs contain information on one taxon.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following statements is incorrect for the reason of opting scientific names over vernacular names?
options: Vernacular names cannot be used in communications.
Some vernacular names have incorrect meaning.
Some vernacular names are particularly used for specific organisms only.
All organisms do not occur in an area.
questions.solution: Vernacular or common names are the names given to the organisms in a particular language and region of the world. Sometimes a single organism is known by several names in the same language, e.g. Water lily has 81 Dutch names. A single name is often used for two or more species. e.g., Touch-me-not is the name for both Impatiens balsamifera (Balsam) and Mimosa pudica.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Evolutionary classification is called
questions.solution: In the Phylogenetic system of classification, the organisms are arranged according to their evolutionary relations.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: ICBN stands for
questions.solution: The International Code of Botanical Nomenclature (ICBN) is a set of rules and recommendations dealing with the formal botanical names given to the plant. The foundations of ICBN are given in a book written by C. Linnaeus named Philosophia Botanica. It is independent of zoological nomenclature.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following branches of biology applies to both plants and animals?
questions.solution: Taxonomy is the branch of biology that is applied to both plants and animals. The classification of plants into various groups is called plant taxonomy or systematic botany. Similarly, the classification of animals is called animal taxonomy or systematic zoology. Entomology is the study of insects. Bacteriology is the study of bacteria.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The correct representation of binomial nomenclature is
questions.solution: As per the binomial system of nomenclature, the botanical name consists of generic epithet. The names are written in italic, generic name begins with a capital letter and the specific name begins with a small letter, e.g.,& Brassica indica.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The classification of organisms based on chromosome number is called
questions.solution: The branch of taxonomy, which is based on cytology, is known as cytotaxonomy. It includes the cytological study of chromosomes, i.e., number morphology, chromosome behaviour, etc.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Taxonomy refers to
questions.solution: Taxonomy is the branch of science concerned with classification, identification and nomenclature. The term is derived from the Greek taxis (“arrangement”) and nomos (“law”). Taxonomy is, therefore, the methodology and principles of systematic botany and zoology and sets up arrangements of the kinds of plants and animals in hierarchies of superior and subordinate groups. Among biologists the Linnaean system of binomial nomenclature, created by Swedish naturalist Carolus Linnaeus in the 1750s, is internationally accepted.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Plant nomenclature means:
options: To give names of plants without any rules
Nomenclature of plants under the international rules
Nomenclature of plants in local language
Nomenclature of plants in english language
questions.solution:
This is a universal system of classification.

Botanical nomenclature& is the formal, scientific naming of plants. It is related to, but distinct from& taxonomy. Plant taxonomy is concerned with grouping and classifying plants; botanical nomenclature then provides names for the results of this process. The starting point for modern botanical nomenclature is& Linnaeus'& Species Plantarum& of 1753. Botanical nomenclature is governed by the& International Code of Nomenclature for algae, fungi, and plants& (ICN), which replaces the& International Code of Botanical Nomenclature& (ICBN).

questions.subject: Botany

options: A herbarium houses dried, pressed and preserved plant specimens.
Botanical gardens have a collection of living plants for reference.
A museum has a collection of photographs of plants and animals.
Key is a taxonomic aid for identification of specimens.
questions.solution: A museum has a collection of dead remains of plants and animals in preserved form for study and reference.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: "Relationships are visualized as evolutionary trees". This statement is related to
questions.solution: The study of the diversity of organisms and evolutionary relationships based on comparative anatomy, ecology, physiology, biochemistry and other fields is known as systematics.

questions.subject: Botany

options: One name given by two scientists
One scientific name consisting of a generic and specific epithet
Two names, one latinised, other of a person
questions.solution: he scientific name of any organism consist of a generic epithet and a specific epithet. Generic name starts with capital letter and specific name with small letter. Both the names are written in Italics or underlined in manuscripts.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A taxon is
options: A taxonomic group of any ranking
questions.solution: The term taxon has been introduced in 1948 which indicates a taxonomic group of any rank. It was first used in 1926 by ‘Adolf Meyer-Abich for animal groups, as a back-formation from the word taxonomy. Herman Johannes Lam in 1948 used it for plants and it was adopted at VII International Botanical Congress, held in 1950.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Select the incorrect statement.
options: A genus comprises of a group of related species which has more characters in common in comparison to species of other genera.
Higher the category, greater is the difficulty of determining the relationship to other taxa at the same level.
Going higher from species to kingdom, the number of common characteristics goes on increasing.
All organisms, including plants and the animal kingdom, have species as the lowest category.
questions.solution: On going up the taxonomic hierarchy from species to kingdom number of an organism goes on increasing and the number of common character goes on decreasing. Species is the most important taxonomic category and individuals of a species share maximum no of common characters.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: According to the taxonomic hierarchy, which of the following statements are correct?
options: Felis and Canis are placed under same family.
Potato and brinjal belong to the same genus.
Classes of plants with few similar characters are assigned to higher category called order.
Panther and Felis domestica are placed in different families.
questions.solution: Potato and brinjal not only belongs to the same family but also to the same genus i.e. Solanum. The scientific name of potato and brinjal is Solanum tuberosum and Solanum melongena respectively. Felis and Canis belong to a different families.

questions.subject: Botany

questions.solution: This is important to be able to distinguish different organisms from each other.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is correct about non-living objects?
options: Show both extrinsic and intrinsic growth
questions.solution: Non-living things show only extrinsic growth or growth from outside, whereas intrinsic growth is a characteristic of living organisms only.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: One of the most important functions of botanical garden is
options: One can observe tropical plants there
They provide the natural habitat for wildlife
They provide a beautiful area for recreation
questions.solution: The botanical garden allows Ex-situ conservation of germplasm.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements carefully and select the correct option.

(a) In zoological parks, conditions similar to natural habitats are provided to the animals.
(b) Keys are generally analytical in nature.
(c) In a herbarium sheet, local names are not mentioned.
(d) Taxonomical aids are useful in knowing bioresources.
questions.solution:
Zoological Parks are protected areas where wild animals are protected by providing conditions as close as possible to natural habitats for public exhibition, for understanding wildlife, recreation and education under ex-situ conservation.

Keys are devices used for identification. They are based on contrasting characters, and separate taxonomic keys are required for each taxonomic category such as family, genus, species. Key is generally analytical in nature and represented by the choice made between two opposite options (contrasting characters). Only one is accepted and the other is rejected.

Herbarium sheets provide common names of the plants.

Taxonomical Aids: Several aids help in taxonomic studies such as herbaria, botanical gardens, museums, zoological parks, monographs, etc. which are helpful in the study of various species of plants, animals and other organisms (that are used in agriculture, forestry, industry) to know bio-resources and biodiversity. Intensive laboratory and field studies are required for the identification of organisms.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Botanical gardens and zoological parks have
options: Collection of endemic living species only
Collection of exotic living species only
Collection of endemic and exotic living species
Collection of only local plants and animals
questions.solution: They are used to collect different species of plants & animals.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Biosystematics aims at
options: Identification and arrangement of organisms on the basis of their cytological characteristics.
The classification of organisms based on broad morphological characters.
Delimiting various taxa of organisms and establishing their relationships.
The classification of organisms based on their evolutionary history and establishing their phylogeny on the totality of various parameters from all fields of studies.
questions.solution: Biosystematics is the study of biological diversity and its origins. It focuses on understanding evolutionary relationships among organisms, species, higher taxa, or other biological entities, such as genes, and the evolution of the properties of taxa including intrinsic traits, ecological interactions, and geographic distributions.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: "Relationships are visualized as evolutionary trees". This statement is related to
questions.solution: The study of the diversity of organisms and evolutionary relationships based on comparative anatomy, ecology, physiology, biochemistry and other fields is known as systematics.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The taxonomic unit 'Phylum' in the classification of animals is equivalent to which hierarchical level in classification of plants?
questions.solution:
Classes comprising animals like fishes, amphibians, reptiles, birds along with mammals constitute the next higher category called Phylum.& In the case of plants, classes with a few similar
characters are assigned to a higher category called Division.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which taxonomical aid provides protection and identification of animals in artificial habitat?
questions.solution: A zoological park is a place where wild animals are kept with human control in the natural environment. A zoo (short form of 'zoological park') is a facility in which animals are housed within enclosures, cared for and displayed to the public. It is a kind of taxonomical aid.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following families are included under order Polymoniales?
options: More than one option is correct
questions.solution: Plant families such as Convolvulaceae, Solanaceae are included in the order Polymoniales mainly based on the floral characters.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A system of classification in which a large number of traits are considered is
questions.solution:
The natural system of classification considers comparable study of a number of characters so as to bring out natural similarities and dissimilarities and hence natural relationships among the organisms.

The system employs characters which are relatively constant. They include morphological characters, anatomical characters, cytological characters, physiology, ontogeny or development, reproduction, cytochemistry and bio­chemistry, experimental taxonomy, etc.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is a division in taxonomical hierarchy?
questions.solution: Taxonomic hierarchy represents categories of classification. It is defined as a sequence of categories in a decreasing or increasing order from kingdom to species and vice versa. The kingdom is the highest rank followed by division, class, order, family, genus and species. In plants, Angiospermae represents the rank of division.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Herbarium is:
options: A garden where medicinal plants are grown
A well-kept storehouse of live and growing herbaceous plants
A storehouse of dried and well-preserved plant specimens
questions.solution: A& herbarium& (plural:& herbaria) is a collection of preserved plant specimens and associated data used for scientific study. The specimens may be whole plants or plant parts; these will usually be in dried form mounted on a sheet of paper but, depending upon the material, may also be stored in boxes or kept in alcohol or other preservatives.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: While correcting the biology paper of a student, the teacher found that he had written the scientific name of mango in four places as follows. Which one out of these is the correct way of writing the scientific name?
questions.solution: Based on the rules of nomenclature, while writing the scientific name, the generic epithet should start with a capital letter, the species epithet should start with a small letter and both should be separately underlined.

questions.solution: On moving up the taxonomical hierarchy number of common characteristics between organism decreases but number on organism goes on increasing. Kingdom has maximum number of organism but similarities between these organism is minimum.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following bracketed keys correctly describes the Whittaker's five kingdom classification?
questions.solution:
According to Whittaker's classification:

Kingdom Monera includes organisms with ill-defined nucleus (prokaryotes).

Kingdom Protista includes organisms with well-defined nucleus (eukaryotes) which have a single cell.

Kingdom Plantae includes multicellular eukaryotes that are autotrophic.

Kingdom Fungi includes multicellular eukaryotes that are saprophytic.

Kingdom Animalia includes multicellular eukaryotes that are holozoic.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is a species?
options: A basic unit in the phylogenic history of living organisms
A group of related populations from evolutionary point of view
A basic category containing most of the taxonomic information
A population of similar characteristics which forms evolutionary basis of variation
questions.solution: Species is the smallest unit of taxonomic hierarchy, which consists of group of similar organism capable of interbreeding freely in nature to form fertile offsprings. It brings about variation necessary for evolution.

questions.subject: Botany

flowers have various colours and scents
questions.solution: Floral feature are more preferred and used for classification of angiosperms as they are more conservative. They are stable and not effected by changing environmental conditions.

These specimens, along with their descriptions on herbarium sheets, become a storehouse or repository for future use.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A natural system of classification based on natural affinities among the organisms, including external and internal features, was given by
questions.solution: The natural classification of plants is based on the external (or morphological) features and internal features (ultrastructure, anatomy, embryology and biochemistry). The classification of angiosperms is given by George Bentham and Joseph Dalton Hooker.& These two English botanists classified plants based on original studies of specimens. They published their well-known scheme of classification in a book Genera plantarum. Especially from the practical point of view, this system of classification is still regarded as the best classification system.

questions.subject: Botany

Select the correct statement from the following given statements.

(II) Properties of cellular organelles are present in the molecular constituents of the organelles and arise as a result of interactions among them.
(III) Living organisms are system capable of responding to external stimuli.
options: I, II and III are correct
questions.solution: Cellular organelles characteristics are not present in the molecular components of the organelle but form as a result of interactions among the molecular components making the organelle. Living organisms are self-replicating, evolving and self-regulating interactive systems capable of responding to external stimuli. Properties of tissues are not presenting the constituent cells but arise as a result of interactions among the constituent cells.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is correct about binomial nomenclature?
options: Both the words in binomial name, when handwritten, are separately underlined.
Both generic name and the specific epithet are printed in italics.
Generic name starts with a small letter and the Specific epithet starts with a small letter.
questions.solution: Biological names are generally in Latin and written in italics. The first word in a biological name represents the genus while the second component denotes the specific epithet. When these words are handwritten, they are separately underlined or printed in italics to indicate their Latin origin. The first word of the genus starts with a capital letter while the specific epithet starts with a small letter.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Rules for Nomenclature are given by certain organizations and are universal. Which one of the following is not a rule for naming an organism?
options: Biological names can be written in any language
The first word in a biological name represents the genus name, and the second is a specific epithet.
The names are written in Latin and are italicized
When written by hand, the names are to be underlined separately.
questions.solution: Biological names are written in Latin only if derived from other languages than they are Latinised. The names are written in italicized to indicate Latin origin. The scientific name consists of two parts the first name is the name of genus and the second is the name of species called a specific epithet.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which statement from below is correct regarding the five kingdom system of classification?
options: Kingdom Protista has brought together Chlamydomonas and Chlorella with Paramoecium and Amoeba.

Five kingdom system of classification brought together the prokaryotic bacteria and blue green algae with other groups which were eukaryotic.
Kingdom Fungi has brought together all heterotrophic organisms.
questions.solution: Chlamydomonas and Chlorella are unicellular eukaryotic photosynthetic organisms. Earlier they were classified under Plantae and were considered unicellular algae. Paramoecium and Amoeba are unicellular eukaryotic heterotrophic organisms. Earlier they were classified under Animalia and were considered protozoans. In the five kingdom classification, all unicellular eukaryotic organisms have been placed under kingdom Protista. Thus Paramoecium, Amoeba, Chlorella and Chlamydomonas have been placed under the same kingdom

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read the following statements and select the correct option.

a. To facilitate more sound and scientific placement of various taxa, taxonomists have also developed subcategories.
b. Only a few protozoans are heterotrophs and live as predators or parasites.
questions.solution:
Taxonomists have developed subcategories to make the taxonomic position of species more precise and specific categories are added to this list. They are called intermediate categories, e.g., subkingdom, superphylum or superdivision, subdivision, superclass, subclass, superorder, suborder, and superfamily subfamily, tribe, subspecies, variety etc.

All protozoans are compulsorily heterotrophic. They derive nutrients from other organisms, by completely ingesting the left out organic remains or waste-products. The protozoans perform phagocytosis and engulf their organic particles by forming pseudopodia or directly taking food through a specialized mouth called cytostome. Protozoans are basically free-living and often found in fresh, brackish, or saltwater. Parasitic and symbiotic protozoans are also present and they live within other organisms.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Sweet potato is a modified root. Potato is a modified stem. Both these plants are classified in order
questions.solution:
Ipomoea batatas or sweet potato is a plant which belongs to the family Convolvulaceae. It is also called the Morning glory Family. Potato belongs to the family Solanaceae. Both are included in the order Polymoniales.

Generally, order and other higher taxonomic categories are identified based on the aggregates of characters. Order is an assemblage of families that exhibit a few similar characters. The similar characters are less in number as compared to different genera included in a family. Plant families like Convolvulaceae, Solanaceae are included in the order polymoniales mainly based on the floral characters.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following statements regarding universal rules of nomenclature is wrong?
options: The first word in a biological name represents the genus
The first word denoting the genus starts with a capital letter
Both the words in a biological name, when handwritten are separately underlined
Biological names are generally in Greek and written in italics
questions.solution:
There are certain rules

(i) The names are in Latin language, sometimes in Greek.

(ii) Generic name begins with the capital letter and is placed before specific name.

The specific name begins with a small letter.

(iii) The scientific name should either be underlined or italicized.

(iv) Name of the authority should be written after specific epithet in an abbreviated from.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: In a hierarchical system of plant classification, which one of the following taxonomic ranks generally ends in 'ceae'?
questions.solution: Family is a taxonomic category between the division and order. It includes one or more genera. It suffix is 'aceae'.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Read these statements about a taxonomic key. How many are false?

$1.$ A taxonomic key is based on the contrasting characters generally in a pair called a couplet.

$2.$ It is generally analytical.

$3.$ It is a taxonomic aid used for identification of plants only.

$4.$ Only accepted statement in the key is called a lead.
questions.solution: A key in taxonomy facilitates the identification of unknown species of an organism based on contrasting characters. It provides a choice between two contradictory statements resulting in acceptance of one and the rejection of the other. A single pair of the contradictory statement is called a couplet and each statement of a couplet is termed a lead (each statement in the key is called a lead). This taxonomic aid is used for all the organisms.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Among the following, increase in body mass can be taken as a criterion for growth:
questions.solution:
Living creatures share some characters which are not found in the non-living.
Growth is one of such features or characteristic property which is present in the living. The numerical changes or structural changes leading to enhancement in the object, in terms of an increase in size, number, volume, mass, etc. are termed as Growth. There are two main types of physiological reactions, Anabolism and Catabolism. When the cell (or living being) makes up (builds) complex material from simple substances, it is called Anabolism. On the contrary, when the living being breaks complex forms into simpler forms, it is termed as Catabolism.
Growth occurs when Anabolism > Catabolism. This is a characteristic feature of living. Growth in living takes place from within (called Intrinsic growth).&
However, non-living beings, such as Mountain, River, Desert, etc. also grows. This is not intrinsic. The growth seen in non-living beings is external or extrinsic. Additional material is deposited outside and there is an increase in area, volume, mass, or size.&

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Members of the same species
options: produce fertile offsprings in natural condition
differ a lot with each other
questions.solution: Species is the smallest unit of taxonomic hierarchy, which consists of group of similar organism capable of interbreeding freely in nature to form fertile offsprings, it brings about variation necessary for evolution.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The order of Homo sapiens is
questions.solution: The classification of all living organism has been done by diving them into different levels based on their features and characteristics. There is a hierarchy in this classification and each step is representing a rank or category known as taxonomic category. There are around seven main taxonomic ranks or categories - species, genus, family, order, class, phylum / division and kingdom. Families which exhibit few similar characters are placed under the same Order. The man (Homo sapiens) belongs to the animal kingdom, division chordate, class mammalia, order primata, family hominidae and genus Homo.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The framework system of classification in which various taxonomic categories are arranged in order of logical sequence is called
questions.solution:
Systematics (L-system: order). The comparative study of organisms based on morphology, anatomy, ecology, physiology, biochemistry, etc. is known as systematics. This comprises three fields such as
1.& & Nomenclature
2.& & Classification and
3.& & Taxonomy

Systematics is also the science of diversity of organisms from an evolutionary context.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Sequence of taxonomic categories is
questions.solution: To construct the hierarchy of classification, one or more species are grouped into a genus, one or more of genera into a family, families are clubbed into order, orders into class, classes into phylum and various phyla into kingdom.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:

$A.$ National Botanical Institute is located at Lucknow.

$B.$ Monographs help in identification of correct species.

$C.$ Muscidae is the order of housefly.
questions.solution:
Examples of some famous Botanical gardens :

$1.$ Botanical garden at Kew, England.

$3.$ National Botanical Research Institute, Lucknow, India.

Few means for recording the descriptions are also helpful in the process of identification of correct specimen e.g. flora, manuals, monographs and catalogues. In monographs description of single taxon is given. Muscidae is the Family of housefly

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Taxonomic studies consider a group of individual organisms with fundamental similarities as a
questions.solution: The classification of all living organism has been done by dividing them into different levels based on their features and characteristics. There is a hierarchy in this classification and each step represents a rank or category known as taxonomic category. There are around seven main taxonomic ranks or categories - species, genus, family, order, class, phylum/division and kingdom. Group of individuals having similar fundamental qualities are called species. When the group of related species have more common characters among them they are referred to as genus. Families which exhibit few similar characters are placed under the same Order. All the fishes, amphibians, reptiles, birds along with mammals constitute the taxonomic level phylum.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which one of the taxonomic aids can give a comprehensive account of complete compiled information of any one genus or family at a particular time?
questions.solution: Taxonomic keys are aids for the rapid identification of unknown plants. Flora is an inventory of the plants of a defined geographical region. A herbarium is a safe place for storing specimens as well as provide a suitable atmosphere for research. A monograph is a comprehensive taxonomic treatment of a taxonomic group, generally a genus or a family, providing all taxonomic data relating to that group.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is incorrectly paired?
questions.solution:
Common Name: Wheat
Binomial name:& Triticum aestivum
Genus: Triticum
Family:& Poaceae
Order:& Poales

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following taxonomical ranks contain organisms least similar to one another
questions.solution: The closely related orders are grouped into a class (named as a taxonomical rank in classification) which have least similar organisms to another.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match the following.
&
Column I Column II
$( P )$ Flora (I) Information for identification of names of species found in an area.
$( Q )$ Manuals (II) Provides an index to plants species found in an area
$( R )$ Monograph (III) Information of one taxon
& (IV) Contains an actual account of habitat and distribution of plants of a given area.
questions.solution: Taxonomy is study of identification and classification of organisms. Taxonomic aids help to store and preserve these organisms. These aids are Herbarium, Botanical gardens, Museum, Zoological parks and keys, Manuals, Monograph, Flora and Catalogues. Flora means information of distribution of plants in a given area. Manuals have information for identification of names of species found in an area. Monographs have taxon information.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A taxon is
options: a taxonomic group of any ranking.
questions.solution: The word taxon signifies a taxonomic group of any rank that represents the real biological organisms included in a category. The term taxon was coined by Adolf Meyer (1926). Basic unit or smallest taxon of taxonomy/classification is species.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Recognize the following flow diagram and find CORRECT option according to taxonomic hierarchy.
questions.solution:
Taxonomy is the branch of biological science which includes nomenclature and classification of the organisms into groups based on their shared features and characteristics. Classification is the process of grouping organisms based on observable features into categories called 'taxa'. The ranks/taxa have the following sequence from largest to the smallest with similarities in organisms increasing at each step. Kingdom, phylum/division, class, order, family, genus and species form the hierarchy in classification where Kingdom is the largest rank and species is the lowest with maximum similarities.

All the plant type names given belong to same group at 6th position which is division Angiospermae.

Of the four plants, wheat is a monocot and rest are dicot. Position 5 is class Monocotyledonae and position 4 is class Dicotyledonae. After class is the order rank and wheat comes in the order Poales.

Mango (Mangifera indica) belongs to the order Sapindales and the genus Datura and Petunia come under the order Polymoniales.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is the correct order in decreasing size in taxonomic hierarchy?
options: Kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus and species.
Kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, species and genus.
Kingdom, phylum, class, species, order, family and genus.
Kingdom, species, phylum, class, order, family and genus.
questions.solution:
Taxonomy is the branch of biological science which includes nomenclature and classification of the organisms into groups based on their shared features and characteristics.

Classification is the process of grouping organisms based on observable features in to categories called 'taxa'. This process involves hierarchy of steps where each taxa represents a rank. All the steps/taxon collectively is referred as taxonomic hierarchy. The ranks/taxa have the following sequence from largest to the smallest with similarities in organisms increasing at each step. Kingdom, phylum, class, order, family, genus and species form the hierarchy in classification where Kingdom is the largest rank and species is the lowest with maximum similarities.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: _________ is a taxonomic category and identified on the basis of aggregates of characters.
questions.solution:
Order and above taxonomic categories based on aggregate of characters.

Order Group of closely related families.
Family Group of closely related genera.
Genus Group of closely related species.
Species Group of individuals with fundamental similarities

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following 'suffixes' is used for "family" in plant classification?
questions.solution: According to ICBN suffixes used for family is -aceae. Name of the family should end with -aceae. For example Fabaceae, Solnaceae, Liliaceae, Brassicaceae.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
How many of the following are taxa at "class" level?
plants, insecta, animals, Mammalia, dicotyledonae, dog, wheat, rice, Jointed legs, Mango
questions.solution: Taxa is a group of organism at any category or rank. Insecta, mammalian, dicotyledonae are taxon at the rank of class.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
From the list of characteristics given, how many of them are defining properties of living organisms?

a) metabolism
b) reproduction
c) cellular organisation
d) consciousness
e) growth
questions.solution:
Three of the given characters are defining properties: reproduction, consciousness, cellular organization.
Growth and metabolism can be observed even outside of living organisms. For example, a mountain can grow over the years.
Similarly, metabolism can be observed in vitro under artificial conditions.&

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is CORRECT about growth?
options: Growth is regarded as one of most fundamental and conspicuous characteristics of living being.
Growth can be defined as an irreversible permanent increase in size of an organ or its parts or even of an individual cell.
Generally, growth is accompanied by metabolic processes (both anabolic and catabolic), that occur at the expense of energy.
questions.solution: All living organisms grow. Growth is permanent and irreversible change in size, shape, volume and dry weight. Growth can be intrinsic and extrinsic. Non-living also grow but their growth is extrinsic (surface growth due to deposition of substances) whereas living organisms exhibit intrinsic growth (internal growth), intrinsic growth results due to metabolic activity. Plants show Indeterminate growth i.e. grow throughout the life while animals grow only up to certain age. Chapter: Plant growth and Development

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: During phylogenetic studies which of the following is sequenced?
questions.solution:
The study of relationships between different groups/species of organisms and their evolutionary development is called phylogeny. It helps in determining the ancestry and evolutionary history of all life forms on Earth.

One of the RNA found in the cell that helps in translation by supporting the protein synthesis organelle ribosomes is the ribosomal RNA (rRNA) which is sent to the cytoplasm from nucleus. rRNA varies between species due to mutation and using its sequence can trace the evolutionary relationships. Also, it is a simpler molecule compared to DNA and its function is same in all organism. Conducting experiments is easier. rRNA study led to the formation of 'Domains' - Bacteria, Archaea and Eukaryotes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The number of common characters among organisms
questions.solution: Maximum similarity occurs in species and this decreases with the increasing rank in the hierarchy. Plantae is the kingdom and is the highest category in the taxonomy that includes all the organisms which share a set of distinguishing characters. Poaceae is the category family and is of higher rank than that of the genus. It consists of one to many related genera, which are more similar to one another than to genera of other families.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The suffix - aceae indicates
questions.solution: In the Linneaus system of the classification there are seven levels that are also called taxa. He is also called the father of modern taxonomy. The taxa are arranged from the largest to the smallest in which family is present between order and genus and that includes one or more genera. Its suffix is -aceae.Example: Brassicaceae, Papaveraceae, Liliaceae, etc. To represent Order suffix should be -ales

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Two organisms with different correlated morphological characters belongs to
questions.solution:
Species is a group of similar individuals which produces offspring's that are fertile and capable of interbreeding.

Theodosius Dobzhansky gave the biological species concept defined as "a species as a group of individuals living in one or more populations that can potentially interbreed to produce healthy, fertile offspring."

Species sharing correlated morphological characters will not be considered as a biological species since they cannot produce fertile offsprings.

A natural taxon having pattern/morphological characters shared by all members of the group is considered as taxonomic species.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The common characteristics between tomato and potato will be maximum at the level of their
questions.solution: Tomato is Lycopersicum esculentum and potato is Solanum tuberosum, both belong to different genus but are members of the same family, thus maximum common characters are observed at the level of the family.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following is not according to the Binomial nomenclature?
options: The first word represents the genus and the second represents species.
The names are written in Latin and are italicized
Biological names can be written in any language
If the name is hand written, it has to be underlined separately.
questions.solution: Biological names are written in Latin only if derived from other languages then they are Latinized. The names are written in italicized to indicate Latin origin. The scientific name consists of two parts the first name is the name of genus and the second is the name of species called as a specific epithet.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following combinations is correct for Wheat?
options: Genus Triticum, family Poaceae, order Poales, Class Dicotyledonae
Genus Triticum, family Poaceae, order Sapindales, class Monocotyledonae.
Genus Triticum, family Poaceae, order Poales, Class Moncotyledonae.
Genus Triticum, family Anacardiaceae, order Poales, class Monocotyledonae
questions.solution: The botanical name of wheat is Triticum aestivum. So the genus of wheat is Triticum. Wheat belongs to the Poaceae or Gramineae family. It is a big and nearly universal family of grasses. The stem of grass is called a culm. The flowers of Poaceae are characteristically arranged in spikelets and enclosed by bracts. Those species come in order Poales they show pollination by winds i.e.anemophily. Single cotyledon is present so they belong to Monocotyledonae class.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Living state is a _____________, __________ state able to perform work.
questions.solution: The living systems are in a metabolic flux and thus they maintain the concentration of biomolecules. Thus they are in non-equilibrium state. This is important because if they reach the equilibrium state, no work will be performed. Hence the living organisms receive an input of energy to prevent reaching an equilibrium state. This energy is received through metabolism (anabolism and catabolism).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: An organism is in the same class but not in the same family. It may belong to same:
options: More than one option is correct
questions.solution:
Taxonomy is the branch of biological science which includes nomenclature and classification of the organisms into groups based on their shared features and characteristics.

Classification is the process of grouping organisms based on observable features in to categories called 'taxa'. This process involves hierarchy of steps where each taxa represents a rank. All the steps/taxon collectively is referred as taxonomic hierarchy.

Species is the basic unit of classification and consist of similar individuals that can interbreed and produce fertile offspring.

Group of related species which has more characters in common in comparison to species of other genera is referred to as genus.

Order is a rank in classification that is higher than family but lower than class.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Which of the following is /are true with reference to taxonomical aids?

a. Separate taxonomic keys are required for each taxonomic category.
b. Keys are not considered to be analytical in nature.
c. Each statement in the key is called a couplet.
d. Keys are used for identification purposes.
questions.solution: Key is a taxonomical aid used for identification of plants and animals based on the similarities and dissimilarities. The keys are based on the contrasting characters generally in a pair called couplet. It represents the choice made between two opposite options. This results in acceptance of only one and rejection of the other. Each statement in the key is called a lead. Separate taxonomic keys are required for each taxonomic category such as family, genus and species for = identification purposes. Keys are generally analytical in nature.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A tautonym is
options: same name for genus and species
common name used as scientific name
questions.solution: A scientific name having the same generic name and specific name is called tautonyms. Tautonyms are accepted for animals but not accepted for plants. Example Ratus ratus, Naja naja, Catla catla.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Select the incorrect statement.
options: The first word in a biological name represents the genus while the second component denotes the specific epithet.
Biological names are generally in the Latin language.

Both the words in a biological name, when handwritten, are
separately underlined, or printed in Latin.
The first word denoting the genus starts with a capital letter& while the specific epithet starts with a small letter.&
questions.solution:
Universal rules of nomenclature are as follows:

1. Biological names are generally in Latin and written in italics. They are Latinised or derived from Latin irrespective of their origin.
2. The first word in a biological name represents the genus while the second component denotes the specific epithet.
3. Both the words in a biological name, when handwritten, are separately underlined, or printed in italics to indicate their Latin origin.
4. The first word denoting the genus starts with a capital letter while the specific epithet starts with a small letter. It can be illustrated with the example of Mangifera indica.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
(i) Aristotle classified plants into herbs, shrubs and trees on the basis of morphology.

(ii) Linnaeus two kingdom classification was based on presence or absence of cell wall.

(iii) R.H. Whittaker include heterotrophic and chitinous cell wall organism in animals.

Select the correct options.
questions.solution: Aristotle was the earliest to attempt a more scientific basis for classification. He used simple morphological characters to classify plants into trees, shrubs and herbs. He also divided animals into two groups, those which had red blood and those that did not. In Linnaeus' time a Two Kingdom system of classification with Plantae and Animalia kingdoms was developed that included all plants and animals respectively. This system did not distinguish between the eukaryotes and prokaryotes, unicellular and multicellular organisms and photosynthetic (green algae) and non-photosynthetic (fungi) organisms.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following statement is wrong regarding the rules of nomenclature?
options: The first word denoting the genus starts with a capital letter.
The specific epithet starts with a small letter.
Biological names are printed in italics to indicate their Latin origin.
In the biological name - Mangifera indica L., 'L' denotes the language 'Latin'.
questions.solution: Rules for naming organism are specified according to specific set of rules. According to binomial nomenclature name of the genus starts with capital letter and name of the species starts with small letter. Scientific names are written in latin language and italics font is used to specific latin origin.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: National Botanical Research Institute is located in
questions.solution: The National Botanical Research Institute(NBRI) is located in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh. It is a research institute of the Council of Scientific and Industrial Research which was originally known as the National Botanical Garden. It is involved in research in areas of plant sciences including taxonomy, genetic engineering, biotechnology and bioinformatics.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: If two organisms can't interbreed to produce fertile offsprings, you can't place them under a
questions.solution: The classification of all living organisms has been done by dividing them into different levels based on their features and characteristics. There is a hierarchy in this classification and each step represents a rank or category known as a taxonomic category. There are around seven main taxonomic ranks or categories - species, genus, family, order, class, phylum/division, and kingdom. Groups of individuals having similar fundamental qualities are called species. Species contain a group of interacting and interbreeding organisms. When the group of related species has more common characters among them they are referred to as genus. Families that exhibit few similar characters are placed under the same Order. All the fishes, amphibians, reptiles, birds along with mammals constitute the taxonomic level phylum.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The unit of classification containing concrete biological entities is
questions.solution: Species are defined as a group of organisms that can sexually produce fertile offspring. There are other parameters that facilitate the classification of the species based on their DNA sequence, morphology, behavior, etc. These organisms share common characteristics with a common gene pool. They have grouped into species based on their morphological or external similarities and more importantly their ability to interbreed.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
How many of the following statement(s) are correct?

(i) Genus comprises a group of related species which has more characters in common in comparison to species.
(ii) 'pardus' and 'leo' are two different species but both belong to the genus Felis.
(iii) Each genus may have one or more than one specific epithets representing different organisms.
(iv) A species is a group of individuals with highest fundamental similarities and maximum number of organisms.
questions.solution: Genus comprises a group of related species which has more characters in common in comparison to species of other genera. pardus and leo are two different species but both belong to the genus Panthera. Each genus may have one or more than one specific epithets representing different organisms, but having morphological similarities. A group of individual organisms with fundamental similarities is species but it has least number of organisms in any given category.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: Isolated metabolic reactions in vitro are not living things but surely living reactions.
All organisms, from the prokaryotes to the most complex eukaryotes have self-consciousness.
The sum total of all the chemical reactions occurring in our body is metabolism.
Metabolic reactions can be demonstrated outside the body in cell-free system.
questions.solution: Consciousness is a defining property because it is seen in all living organisms from prokaryotes to complex eukaryotes without any exception but self-consciousness is a characteristic feature of human only because a human is the only organism which is aware of himself. All reactions taking place inside the body are collectively called metabolism which is also a defining property of living beings.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: All organisms are& ‘aware’ of their surroundings. Hence, all organisms can
options: arise as a result of interactions among the molecular components
be linked to one another by the sharing of the common genetic material
questions.solution: All organisms handle chemicals entering their bodies. All organisms, therefore, are ‘aware’ of their surroundings. A human being is the only organism who is aware of himself, i.e., has self-consciousness. Consciousness, therefore, becomes the defining property of living organisms.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Identify the correct option for the systematic position of mango.
options: Family - Poaceae, order - Poales, class - Monocotyledonae
Family - Anacardiaceae, order - Poales, class - Dicotyledonae
Family - Anacardiaceae, order - Sapindales, class - Dicotyledonae
Family - Poaceae, order - Sapindales, class - Monocotyledonae
questions.solution: The scientific name of mango is Mangifera indica. Mangifera is genus and indica is species. Mango is included in family Anacardiaceae, order Sapindales, class Dicotyledonae and division Angiospermae. In Family Poaceae, wheat and some other grains are included. Wheat is included in order Poales and class Monocotyledonae. The scientific name of wheat is Triticum aestivum.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: What is a herbarium?
options: Store house of collected plant specimen
Store house of collected animal specimen
questions.solution:
Preserved plant specimen and the information regarding the same is collected and stored in a herbarium. In in the stored specimen may be whole plant itself or parts of it. Generally the plant parts are mounted on a sheet of paper in their dried form (exsiccatae).

Fungal preservation collection is generally termed a fungarium.

Animal specimen are generally stored in museums for scientific study and research.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The index to the plant species found in a& particular area is provided in:
questions.solution: Flora contains the actual account of habitat and distribution of plants of a given area. These provide the index to the plant species found in a particular area. Manuals are useful in providing information for identification of names of species found in an area. Monographs contain information on any one taxon.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Rules for Nomenclature are given by certain organizations and are universal. Which one of the following is not a rule for naming an organism?
options: Biological names should be in Latin
The first word in a biological name represents the genus name, and the second is a specific epithet
The names are written in italicized font.
When written by hand, the names are to be underlined together with epithet.
questions.solution: Biological names are written in Latin language, if written in other languages it should be Latinised. Names are written in italics font to indicate Latin origin, if handwritten the names should be separately underlined. The first name represents name of genus and second name is name of species.& When written by hand, the names are to be underlined separately.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The earliest attempt to the scientific basis for classification is made by
questions.solution: Aristotle was a Greek philosopher who classified the living organisms on a scientific basis for the first time. He classified the plants as herbs, shrubs and trees and animals were categorized into two groups, animals with red blood and animals without red blood. The need for a higher and a better classification was always felt. Linnaeus was responsible for the two kingdom classification (Plantae and Animalia) and R.H.Whittaker introduced the five-kingdom classification whose main basis was the mode of nutrition. Theophrastus was a successor to Aristotle and was known for classifying plants and how they reproduced.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Scientific nomenclature of the plant is Rosa indica L. The letter 'L' corresponds to:
options: The name was derived from Latin
It is a long variety of plant
The name was coined by Linnaeus
The plant is found in London
questions.solution: The letter 'L' in Rosa indica indicates the name of the author. i.e Linnaeus (mention the author name after the species name is known as citation)

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Reproduction is characteristic of living organisms. Which of these organisms do not reproduce by fragmentation?
questions.solution: In multicellular organisms, reproduction refers to the production of progeny possessing features more or less similar to those of parents. Invariably and implicitly we refer to sexual reproduction. Organisms reproduce by asexual means also. In Planaria (flatworms), we observe true regeneration, i.e., a fragmented organism regenerates the lost part of its body and becomes a new organism. The fungi, the filamentous algae, the protonema of mosses, all easily multiply by fragmentation. When it comes to unicellular organisms like bacteria, unicellular algae or Amoeba, reproduction is synonymous with growth, i.e., increase in number of cells.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Who from the following first proposed the natural system of classification?
questions.solution: The natural classification systems developed are based on the natural affinities among the organisms and considered,& not only the external features but also internal features, like ultrastructure, anatomy, embryology, and phytochemistry. Such a classification of flowering plants was given by George Bentham and Joseph Dalton Hooker.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: Systematics involves
questions.solution: The study of the historical relationship of groups of biological organisms is called systematics or it is a branch of science that deals with classification or nomenclature. It is a Latin word in which organisms are arranged in a systematic manner. It deals with the population, species, and higher taxa. So the correct answer is D.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: The taxonomic unit 'Phylum' is used in the classification of animals only, which term is equivalent to a phylum in the classification of plants?
questions.solution: In a taxonomical hierarchy, term phylum is used only for animal kingdom. In plant kingdom, term division is used in place of the phylum. According to ICBN specific suffix has been specified for different categories. Name of the division should end with suffix - phyta.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q: A homonym is
options: Two or more names for the same taxon
Species name repeats the generic name
Identical name of two different species
Name given to a taxon in local language
questions.solution: The identical name of two different taxa is called homonym. There is a rule in the International code of zoological nomenclature is that first name to be published in the senior homonym that should be used and the other names are junior homonyms that must be replaced with new names.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
With reference to taxonomical aids, correct statements are

A. Each statement in the key is called a couplet.
B. Herbarium is a storehouse of collected plant and animal specimens.
C. Separate taxonomic keys are required for each taxonomic category.
D. Keys are used for identification purposes.
questions.solution:
Key is a type of taxonomical aid that is used for the identification of both plants and animals based on the similarities and dissimilarities. Usually, for each taxonomic category like species, genus, family, etc., separate taxonomic keys are required.

Each statement in the key is called Lead while a pair of keys based on contrasting characters is called a couplet. The herbarium is a store house of collected plant specimens that are dried, pressed and preserved on sheets.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.q:
Match the taxonomical tools and its explanation between column - I and column - II:
&
& & Column - I & & Column - II
& a. & Museum & (i) Information on one taxon.
& b. & Herbarium & (ii) Couplet.
& c. & Monograph & (iii) A store house of collected plant specimens.
& d. & Taxonomic key & (iv) Educational institutes.
& & & (v) Records of local flora.
questions.solution:
Museum: Biological museums are generally set up in educational institutes such as schools and colleges.
Herbarium: Herbarium is a storehouse of collected plant specimens that are dried, pressed and preserved on sheets.
Taxonomic key: Key is another taxonomical aid used for identification of plants and animals based on the similarities and dissimilarities. The keys are based on the contrasting characters generally in a pair called a couplet.
Monographs: It contains information on any one taxon.
